title: Canary Rollout Runbook — Q2 2026 Draft
body:
Purpose:
This working doc is a runbook for the planned canary-driven rollout pattern for Q2 2026 platform releases. It combines the release engineering checklist, a compact rollout calendar (milestones and guardrails), and a first-pass release-notes draft suitable for product/ops review.

Scope and goals:
- Target: hosted API + Dedicated control-plane changes (no customer DB migrations).
- Primary goals: no customer-facing errors >0.05% p95 error rate during canary window, latency regressions <5% vs baseline, automated rollback within 25 minutes if SLOs breached.
- Secondary: validate telemetry and cost metrics for Redwood Optimize features in a production subset.

High-level timeline (calendar):
- Week 1 (2026-04-06 to 2026-04-10): Final integration + golden CI run. Freeze artifacts by EOD Thu 2026-04-09.
- Week 2 (2026-04-13): Internal dogfood canary (engineering only) — 6 hours, daytime window PST.
- Week 3 (2026-04-20): External canary #1 — 1% traffic, 4-hour window (08:00–12:00 PT).
- Week 4 (2026-04-27): External canary #2 — 10% traffic, 24-hour window.
- Week 5 (2026-05-04): Ramp to 50% traffic, 48-hour window; evaluate for full rollout.
- Week 6 (2026-05-11): Full rollout to 100% (if green) or rollback to previous model/cluster.
Notes: windows chosen to avoid major customer peak hours (EMEA morning). All dates tentative — team signoff required during Week 1.

Pre-release checklist (must be completed before any canary):
- PRs: All GH PRs merged to release branch and reviewed; tagged with release-id: release/q2-2026-0420.
- CI: Passing integration tests and 1x golden run with production-like config. Golden artifacts uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-artifacts/releases/q2-2026-0420/.
- Infra: Canary cluster sized for 2x expected CPU but limited GPU to match production memory profiles. Sizing doc & terraform diff reviewed (PR #2983).
- Feature flags: Create canary flag (feature:canary_q2_2026) and set default off for 100% traffic; verify toggle in console and API.
- Secrets/KMS: Ensure new KMS key rotates are applied and deploys reference the correct key alias.
- Observability: Dashboards cloned and annotated: latency-p95, completion-error-rate, token-cost-per-request, model-GPU-util. Slack alert channels stubbed: #release-alerts and #sre-oncall.
- Rollback artifacts: Previous release container images and model bundles are promoted to 'hot-rollback' registry and smoke-tested.

Canary rollout step-by-step (operational playbook):
- Step 0: Preflight (1 hour before window)
  - Confirm on-call roster for SRE, serving-runtime engineer, release engineer, and product owner.
  - Confirm links and runbooks in #release-ops pinned message.
  - Run quick smoke tests against staging using curl and SDK harness (scripts/release/smoke.sh).

- Step 1: Deploy to canary pool
  - Trigger deployment via release pipeline (GH action: release/deploy-canary).
  - Verify health of pods/instances (kubectl/eksctl checks or equivalent).
  - Activate feature flag to route percentage (start at 1%).

- Step 2: Monitor 0–15 minutes (initial stabilization)
  - Key metrics to observe: 5m error-rate (api.errors), p95-latency (api.latency_p95), request throughput, GPU mem pressure, KV cache hit rate.
  - If any alert fires (see alert thresholds below) go to Incident Decision matrix.

- Step 3: Progressive increments
  - After 4 hours at 1% with no alerts, increase to 5%.
  - After 12 hours at 5% with no alerts/regressions, increase to 10% (external canary #2).
  - Continue to 50% only after 24h at 10% with validated cost and latency.
  - Full rollout only after product sign-off.

Alert thresholds (automated):
- Critical (auto-rollback): API error-rate >0.5% sustained for 5 minutes OR p95-latency > 2x baseline for 10 minutes.
- High (manual review): API error-rate >0.2% for 10 minutes OR token-cost-per-request > 20% increase vs baseline for 30 minutes.
- Observability gaps (blocker): missing telemetry heartbeat for <metrics ingestion> for 3 consecutive minutes — abort and rollback.

Incident Decision matrix (quick):
- Critical alert -> Immediately flip traffic back to previous variant (rollback), page SRE and release lead, open an incident in PagerDuty.
- High alert -> Pause any ramp, open war-room Slack huddle, run targeted small-sample diffs, consider rollback if root cause unclear within 60 minutes.
- Non-critical anomalies -> Log detailed traces, mark for follow-up in post-release review; continue canary if trends remain flat.

Rollback procedure (target: <25 minutes from trigger):
1) Announce rollback in #release-ops with reason and timestamp.
2) Flip traffic routing to previous stable release through traffic-router API or feature flag.
3) Deploy hot-rollback artifact only if routing flip not possible.
4) Run verification smoke tests against stable version (scripts/release/smoke-verify.sh).
5) Update incident ticket and schedule postmortem if outage or significant regression occurred.

Operational notes and known risks:
- KV cache warmup: first 10 minutes typically high-latency due to cold KV cache — expect an initial spike but not sustained p95 regressions. Monitor cache-hit-rate closely.
- Quantized model path: This release includes a new quantization profile for medium-length prompts; verify quality sample set (evals/quant-med-prompts.csv) during canary.
- Cross-region failover: If region-level saturation is observed, fall back to routing policy 'region-aware' which splits traffic to next closest region; this should be manual unless pre-approved.

Release notes (draft) — short form for product and blog snippet:
Title: Q2 2026 — Inference runtime improvements and canary scheduling\nShort summary: This release introduces performance improvements in the serving runtime (optimized attention kernels and KV cache prefetch), an updated quantization profile for medium-length prompts, and several stability fixes for routing and autoscaling. We are rolling out gradually using a canary-first approach to validate latency, error rates, and cost impacts before full traffic migration.
User-facing highlights:
- Up to 12% lower p95 latency for medium-length prompts in tested workloads.
- Reduced variance in tail latency under bursty traffic.
- New cost-optimization toggle for batch scheduling in Redwood Optimize (off by default).
Notes for admins: No customer-facing API surface changes. Dedicated customers on reserved pools will see the performance changes after rollouts; no config changes required. For Private deployments, follow upgrade docs in Confluence (linked).

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Confirm exact list of smoke-test prompts that represent edge-case failure modes (Priya to finalize by 2026-03-12).
- Decide on roll-forward window tolerance for token-cost spikes (proposal: 15% threshold) — product + finance to sign off.
- Finalize communication plan to Dedicated customers (SE-runbook + email templates) — Marcus to draft.

Appendix — quick commands and links:
- Canary deploy pipeline: GH Actions -> Releases -> release/q2-2026-0420 -> Deploy Canary
- Smoke test scripts: repo/scripts/release/smoke.sh and smoke-verify.sh
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/rollout/canary-q2-2026
- PagerDuty runbook: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/new?service=serving-runtime

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep canary windows during PST daytime so east-coast customers are lower risk; double-check holidays.
- If we see noise in cache-hit metrics, don't immediately jump to rollback — correlate with request skew.
- Keep release artifacts immutable post-freeze.

End of draft. This is intentionally iterative — expect edits during Week 1 integration and after first dogfood canary.
